agent.summary:
Done. Here's what changed and what the tests cover.

**`ranking.py`** — two-line change:
- `ORDERING` is now `"popular"`.
- `rank` sorts by `(likes, created_at, id)` descending, so the most-liked post always comes first. Ties on likes fall back to recency, then to ID, keeping the order deterministic.

**`tests/test_popular_ranking.py`** — eight tests:

| Test | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `test_ordering_label_is_popular` | `ORDERING == "popular"` |
| `test_more_liked_post_ranks_first` | Higher likes beats newer `created_at` |
| `test_like_count_beats_recency` | Explicit newer-but-unpopular vs older-but-popular case |
| `test_equal_likes_broken_by_recency_then_id` | Tie-breaking falls to `created_at` then `id` |
| `test_rank_does_not_mutate_input` | Input list and dicts are unchanged |
| `test_api_ordering_field_is_popular` | `GET /api/posts` returns `"ordering": "popular"` |
| `test_api_feed_is_sorted_by_likes_descending` | Live feed order matches descending like counts |
| `test_health_reports_popular_ordering` | Both `/health` and `/api/health` report `"popular"` |
